- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to cap peak; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to reflect cooling.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates momentum; cap forecast growth at 1.5–2% above recent 7-day avg.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to align with historical 30-day mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underpredicts late-period (last 7–10 days) price increases; apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.30 or more), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment shift.
